transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Hi, Doctor. Thank you so much for seeing me, I really appreciate you taking the time. I hope I'm not wasting your time—it's probably nothing major, really—but my wife actually suggested I come in. 

What really brought me in is... well, she’ll be telling me about things, like my cousin’s appointments or coordinating rides, just normal day-to-day stuff. And I’m looking right at her, you know? I'm really trying my best to be a good husband and listen. But then a minute later, I realize I didn’t actually take in half of what she just said. I feel awful about it, because I don't want her to think I don't care. It just sort of... slips by me, I guess. Does that make sense? I hope I'm explaining that right.
Were you having similar attention or concentration problems when you were a child?

Oh, um... well, I suppose so, yes. I mean, I was always a very well-behaved kid, I really never wanted to cause any trouble for my teachers or anything. But, looking back... even in grade school, you know, before I was 12 or so, my teachers would always tell my parents that I was a bright boy. Which was very nice of them to say, of course. 

But they did usually mention that I was... well, maybe a bit of a daydreamer. I would accidentally leave my homework inside my desk, or I'd need a little nudge, just a gentle reminder to finish up my classwork. It wasn't that I was trying to be difficult or lazy, I just sort of drifted off into my own world, I guess. Is that the sort of thing you mean? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right information.
Have you been feeling down or depressed most days lately?

Oh, no, no, not at all. I mean, I hope I don't come across that way. I actually feel pretty content most days, honestly. My wife and I have a nice life, and I wouldn't want to complain when I have so much to be grateful for. 

I mean, sure, I get a little frustrated with myself when I forget things or when I feel like I'm letting her down by not paying attention. That bothers me, of course, because I want to be a good partner. But depressed? No, I wouldn't say that. I really try to stay positive and look on the bright side. I hope that's a good thing, right? I just want to be sure I'm answering you correctly.
Did your attention or concentration problems begin before age 12?

Oh, yes. I'm sorry, I might not have been very clear when I was talking about grade school just a moment ago—I know I can ramble a bit sometimes, so I apologize if I confused things! 

But yes, it was definitely before I was 12 years old. That's when my teachers were mentioning the daydreaming and things like that to my parents. I hope that answers it properly for your notes? I just want to make sure I'm giving you exactly what you need.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about many different things most days?

Oh, um, no, not excessively, I don't think. I mean, I worry a little bit, like anyone else would, I suppose. Just the normal things—making sure the bills are paid on time, hoping my wife is doing well, that sort of everyday stuff. 

I really try not to let things get to me too much. I don't want to be a burden or a, you know, a "worrywart" to the people around me. So, no, I wouldn't say I worry about a lot of different things most days. I try to just take things as they come. Is that... does that sound about right for what you're asking? I want to make sure I'm giving you the right idea.
Have these attention problems gotten noticeably worse only in the past few months?

Well, um, actually, it's been a little bit longer than just a few months. I hope I'm not making a mountain out of a molehill, but... it's been noticeably harder for about 11 months now. 

That was right around the time my cousin moved in with us after having a surgery. We were more than happy to help out, of course! I really don't want to sound like I'm complaining about family, because we love having company and being supportive. But just with the extra, you know, commotion and change in routine in the house, it's made it a bit tougher for me to keep my focus and stay on track. 

I hope it's alright that I bring that up? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the most accurate timeline for your notes. Does that make sense?
Have you also been having trouble remembering recent events or conversations?

Oh, no, I wouldn't say that. My memory is actually pretty good, thankfully! I mean, I might forget where I put my glasses every now and then, but that's just normal for someone my age, right? 

I definitely remember conversations and things that have happened recently. I try very hard to pay attention when people are talking to me—I'd hate for anyone to think I didn't care about what they were saying. So, no, no real trouble with my memory at all. I hope that's a good thing to hear? I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right kind of answers.
